title: Glass Atrium Natural Ventilation Analyzer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D glass atrium natural ventilation analyzer using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a large glass atrium structure: a rectangular building footprint (20x20 units base, 15 units tall) with transparent glass walls (MeshPhysicalMaterial, transmission=0.85, roughness=0.05, ior=1.52, color=#88ccff) and a pitched glass roof (two angled planes meeting at a ridge, peak at 20 units).
- The atrium has 4 operable vent openings: 2 lower intake vents on the north wall (at y=1, each 3x2 units) and 2 upper exhaust vents near the roof ridge (at y=17, each 3x2 units). Represent vents as rectangular planes that rotate open/closed.
- Place a ground plane with a tiled floor texture (procedural checkerboard, warm gray tones).
- Load the 'robot.glb' model using GLTFLoader and place it at the center of the atrium floor (position 0, 0, 0) scaled to approximately 2 units tall. This represents a maintenance robot that monitors ventilation.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional sun light (intensity 1.2, position 10,25,10, casting shadows), and a subtle hemisphere light (sky=#87CEEB, ground=#8B7355, intensity 0.3).
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (30, 20, 30) looking at (0, 8, 0). Add OrbitControls.

VENTILATION PHYSICS:
- Simulate stack-effect natural ventilation. The driving force is temperature difference between interior and exterior.
- Interior temperature starts at 32°C, exterior at 22°C. Temperature difference (deltaT) drives airflow.
- Airflow rate Q (m³/s) = Cd * A_eff * sqrt(2 * g * H_stack * deltaT / T_avg), where Cd=0.61, g=9.81, H_stack = vertical distance between inlet and outlet centers (16 units = 16m), T_avg in Kelvin.
- A_eff = effective vent area = (A_inlet * A_outlet) / sqrt(A_inlet² + A_outlet²). Each vent area = 3*2 * openFraction (0 to 1). Total inlet area = 2 vents * individual area. Same for outlet.
- Ventilation cools the interior: each simulation tick (every 100ms), reduce interior temp by (Q * 0.05) degrees, but interior temp cannot go below exterior temp.
- Visualize airflow with animated particle streams (small blue spheres or sprites) flowing from lower vents upward through the atrium and out upper vents. Particle speed proportional to Q. No particles when vents are closed.
- The robot model should slowly rotate to face the direction of strongest airflow (toward the open lower vents).

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Keyboard '1'/'2': Toggle lower vent 1 / lower vent 2 open/closed (animate rotation 0 to 90 degrees over 0.3s).
- Keyboard '3'/'4': Toggle upper vent 3 / upper vent 4 open/closed.
- Keyboard 'R': Reset all vents closed and interior temp to 32°C.
- A DOM button 'Set Exterior Temp' with an input field (id='exteriorTempInput') and button (id='setTempBtn') to change exterior temperature (valid range 10-40°C).
- Keyboard 'S': Toggle solar heat gain on/off. When on, interior temp increases by 0.1°C per tick (simulating solar radiation through glass), competing with ventilation cooling.
- Click on the robot model to trigger a 'diagnostic pulse': briefly highlight all open vents in green for 1 second.

HUD / UI:
- Top-left HUD panel (id='hudPanel') showing: Interior Temp (id='hudInteriorTemp'), Exterior Temp (id='hudExteriorTemp'), Airflow Rate Q (id='hudAirflow', 2 decimal places), Effective Vent Area (id='hudVentArea'), Vent statuses (id='hudVentStatus', e.g. 'Open: 1,3 | Closed: 2,4'), Solar gain status (id='hudSolarStatus').
- Style HUD with semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font.

STATE MANAGEMENT - Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- interiorTemp: number (current interior temperature in °C)
- exteriorTemp: number (current exterior temperature in °C)
- vents: array of 4 objects [{id:1, open:bool, openFraction:number}, ...] (openFraction 0.0-1.0)
- airflowRate: number (Q in m³/s, 0 when all vents one side closed)
- effectiveVentArea: number (A_eff in m²)
- particleCount: number (active airflow particles)
- solarGainActive: boolean
- robotLoaded: boolean (true after GLB loads)
- robotRotationY: number (robot's current Y rotation in radians)
- diagnosticActive: boolean (true during diagnostic pulse)
- ventOpenCount: number (how many vents are currently open)
- deltaT: number (interiorTemp - exteriorTemp)
- simulationRunning: boolean (true after init)
- tickCount: number (increments each simulation tick)
physics_constraints: Stack-effect ventilation: Q = Cd * A_eff * sqrt(2 * g * H * deltaT / T_avg). Interior temp decreases proportional to airflow. Interior temp >= exterior temp always. Airflow is zero if either all inlets or all outlets are closed. Solar gain adds 0.1°C/tick when active. Effective area uses combined orifice formula.
